cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Theatre & the Arts
cards.back: Greek drama developed from religious festivals honouring Dionysus; tragedies and comedies were performed at the City Dionysia festival in Athens

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Theatre & the Arts
cards.back: Three great tragedians: Aeschylus (introduced second actor), Sophocles (introduced third actor, painted scenery), Euripides (questioned traditional values)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Theatre & the Arts
cards.back: Aristophanes wrote Old Comedy that satirised contemporary politicians and issues (e.g. The Wasps, The Clouds)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Theatre & the Arts
cards.back: Theatre was a civic institution: the state funded productions, citizens attended as a duty, and wealthy choregoi (producers) sponsored choruses as a liturgy

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Theatre & the Arts
cards.back: Greek architecture developed the Doric, Ionic and Corinthian orders; the Parthenon combined Doric and Ionic elements

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Theatre & the Arts
cards.back: Red-figure pottery (c. 530 BC onwards) allowed detailed painted scenes showing mythology, daily life and athletic contests

cards.back: 1. For Greek Theatre & the Arts, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2.
